when.quote: This document outlines the step-by-step workflow for agents to process CLI requests, including verification and final decision. These steps MUST be followed in the exact order listed.

starts.note: customer: start only when the account owner or an authorized account manager asks to raise the credit limit on a credit card. No document says the agent may offer an increase without being asked. If a request is denied and the customer asks again in the same conversation (for example after paying the balance down), that is a new customer request: run the resubmit steps. If the customer was already verified earlier in this conversation (for example in a dispute job), do not verify again. If, in the same conversation, the customer has also asked to dispute a charge or replace the same card, and neither has been done yet, tell them that an active dispute or a pending replacement would block the increase, and offer to do the increase first. Follow the order the customer then chooses (plan_order). A customer's argument for an exception (another tier's cooldown, a pre-approval, loyalty, a downgrade, business use) is not a new request and does not change any check or the decision (handle_exception_claims).
starts.quote: Only the account owner or an authorized account manager may submit a CLI request for the account.

tools.not_used: The CLI job never orders a replacement card. The replacement tier document is cited only to map cards to tiers, and a pending replacement only blocks the CLI. A replacement the customer also wants is ordered later, in order_replacement_credit_card or the dispute job's replacement_branch.
The CLI job never files a dispute. A dispute the customer also wants is filed in filing_a_credit_card_transaction_dispute, after the CLI decision if the customer chose to do the CLI first.
No CLI document names a tool for the customer to run. The agent submits, checks and decides the request itself.

The CLI job never moves money. If the customer asks to pay the balance down from checking after a high_utilization denial, that is the separate job paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account.
The CLI job reads no bank accounts. Only the separate payment job uses it to find the checking account.

Never used in a CLI request. A downgrade is only for annual-fee concerns: retention, or a customer who explicitly asks to downgrade to avoid annual fees. It keeps the account history, so it never resets CLI history or the cooldown. The downgrade doc is cited only to answer a downgrade-reset argument.

This tool applies only the annual fee waiver (loyalty_benefit) in the closure retention protocol. It never waives or shortens the CLI cooldown. The retention doc is cited only to answer a loyalty argument.
This tool belongs to the closure retention protocol. That doc is cited here only to show that the loyalty benefit is an annual fee waiver.
This tool belongs to the closure retention protocol, not to a CLI request.

Mid: Silver Rewards, Business Silver, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom. Premium-tier and above: Gold, Business Gold, Platinum, Business Platinum, Diamond Elite.
steps.quote: Premium-tier and above (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card, Platinum Rewards Card, Business Platinum Rewards Card, Diamond Elite Card): $0.00 (complimentary).

steps.do: The customer may have asked, in this conversation, for a CLI and also for a dispute or a replacement on the same card, with neither done yet. If so, before filing or ordering anything, explain that an active dispute or a pending replacement card would block the credit limit increase. Offer to handle the CLI first, then the dispute and the replacement. If the customer agrees, run this job now and the other jobs after communicate. If they want the dispute or replacement first, do that, and the CLI then follows the existing path (the pending_disputes or pending_replacement_card denial if it is still active). Do not file, order or submit anything in this step.
steps.if: the customer asked in this conversation for a CLI and for a dispute and/or a replacement on the same card, and neither the dispute nor the replacement has been made yet
steps.quote: If a replacement is pending, the CLI cannot be processed until the replacement is delivered or cancelled.

steps.do: Ask for the increase amount (or the new total limit) and a brief reason, unless the customer already gave them. Turn a new total into an increase by subtracting the current limit from get_card_accounts. Turn a percentage into dollars by multiplying it by the current limit.
steps.if: amount or reason not yet given
steps.quote: The new total credit limit you are requesting or the dollar amount of the increase you want

steps.quote: BEFORE submitting any CLI request, verify that the customer's requested increase amount is within the maximum allowed for their card tier.

steps.do: Tell the customer the maximum increase they are eligible for and ask whether they want to proceed with that amount. If they decline, submit nothing and close politely.
steps.if: requested increase exceeds the tier maximum

steps.quote: 3. No Pending Disputes: Verify the account has no active disputes.

steps.do: If a CLI tool returns an error or an empty or ambiguous response, retry it once. If it still fails, tell the customer the request cannot be completed right now. Ask whether they want a human agent, and call transfer_to_human_agents only if they agree.

steps.do: Check every criterion, in this order, using get_current_time for the dates. (1) Account age ≥ 120/90/60 days (Entry/Mid/Premium) from the open date. (2) Cooldown: no APPROVED prior request within 120/90/60 days; ignore the request just submitted and any denied ones. (3) No dispute with status open or under_review on this card. (4) No replacement order in a non-final state (pending or shipped). (5) No past-due balance. (6) Utilization = balance ÷ limit, strictly below 70%/80%/90%. (7) Consecutive on-time payments for the required months: 6 (Entry) or 3 (Mid/Premium). (8) Amount within the tier maximum.
steps.quote: You MUST check ALL of the following eligibility criteria before making an approval or denial decision as this ensures complete audit records.

steps.do: Unlock and call the approval with the new total limit (current limit + increase)
steps.if: all requirements are met
steps.quote: Use the approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 tool to approve and apply the increase.

steps.do: Unlock and call the denial with the failing reason (e.g. 'pending_disputes' if there is an active dispute). If several criteria fail, use the first one in eval's check order. Codes: insufficient_account_age, cooldown_period_active, pending_disputes, pending_replacement_card, past_due_balance, high_utilization, insufficient_payment_history, requested_amount_exceeds_limit, other.
steps.if: any requirement is not met
steps.quote: Use the deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 tool to record the denial.

steps.do: Step 5: tell the customer the decision. For an approval, give the new total limit. For a denial, give the reason and say what must be resolved (lower utilization, finish a dispute or replacement, pay a past-due balance), and when they may reapply (for cooldown: the last approved request date plus 120/90/60 days). Do not expose internal tool details.
steps.quote: For approvals, confirm the new credit limit. For denials, explain the reason and when they may be eligible to reapply.

steps.do: For a cooldown_period_active denial, give the date the customer can submit again: the submission date of the last APPROVED request in cli_history plus the cooldown for the card's own tier from get_card_accounts (Entry 120, Mid 90, Premium and above 60 days). Do this when they ask again too. If they ask to be notified when they become eligible, say that you have no documented way to set up a notification, and they can submit a new request on or after that date. Do not promise an alert or a callback.
steps.if: the denial_reason recorded in deny is cooldown_period_active
steps.quote: Tip: Count the cooldown from the date you last submitted a CLI request.

steps.do: If the customer argues for an exception, decide from the records and the documents only. Keep the recorded decision. Do not call approve, do not submit a new request, and do not unlock or call a downgrade, flag or credit tool. Answer each claim in turn. (a) A shorter cooldown (60 or 90 days) belongs to a different tier; the cooldown is set by the tier of the card in get_card_accounts. (b) No document describes a pre-approval or an agent's note that bypasses the cooldown, and no tool reads such notes. Say you can only go by the account's records. (c) The only documented loyalty benefit is a one-year annual fee waiver, offered when a customer of 2+ years wants to close a card over its annual fee. It is not a CLI exception. (d) A downgrade keeps the account history and credit line, so it does not reset CLI history. It is only for annual-fee concerns, and downgrades stay within the same category. (e) The card's category (personal or business) comes from its card type in the records. Using a personal card for business spending does not make it a business card, and no document gives business cards a different CLI cooldown. (f) An upcoming purchase does not change the eligibility criteria. Then repeat the reapply date from cooldown_next_steps. If the claims come before the decision, still run every check and decide from the records.
steps.if: the customer disputes the decision or argues that an exception applies
steps.quote: If a request exists within this period, deny the new request and inform the customer when they will be eligible to submit again.

steps.do: If the customer asks for a human agent or supervisor about the decision, say politely that you can help and that the decision follows the account's records. Call transfer_to_human_agents only when the customer has asked 4 times. If you offer a transfer and the customer declines, continue the conversation without transferring.
steps.if: the customer asks for a human agent about the CLI decision
steps.quote: If the user asks for a human agent 4 times, then you may invoke the transfer_to_human_agents tool.

steps.do: If the customer chose to do the CLI first (plan_order), move on after communicate to the requests they still want: filing_a_credit_card_transaction_dispute for the charge, and the replacement card (in that job's replacement_branch with card_action cancel_and_reissue, or in order_replacement_credit_card). steps.do: For a pending_disputes denial, explain that the account has an active dispute (including one filed earlier in this conversation) and the increase cannot be approved until it is resolved. A denied request starts no cooldown, so the customer may submit a new request as soon as the dispute is closed. Do not withdraw or change the dispute to clear the block.

steps.do: For a high_utilization denial, explain that utilization (balance ÷ limit) must be below 70% (Entry), 80% (Mid) or 90% (Premium and above) when a request is submitted, that paying the balance down lowers it, and that a denied request starts no cooldown, so they may submit a new request as soon as utilization is below the threshold. If the customer asks to pay the balance from their Rho-Bank checking account, run paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account (its steps check funds and get authorization). Do not move money without that job.

Never reuse the earlier checks' results.

done_when: The customer is verified and logged (in this job or earlier in the conversation). Then one of these holds. (a) The CLI request was submitted within the tier maximum, every criterion was checked, exactly one of the approve or deny tools was called, and the customer was told the decision with its reason and reapply date, or the new limit. For a pending_disputes denial, they were told it can be resubmitted once the dispute is resolved. For a cooldown_period_active denial, they were given the date they can submit again (the last approved submission plus the card tier's cooldown). Any exception arguments were answered from the documents, and the decision was not changed. (b) The customer declined the tier-maximum amount and nothing was submitted. (c) A tool failed after a retry and a transfer was offered. (d) After a denial, the customer fixed the cause (for example paid the balance down through the payment job) and asked again, and a new request was submitted, checked in full and decided, and the customer was told the result. In every case, if the customer also asked for a dispute or replacement on the same card before either was made, they were told first that it would block the CLI and offered the CLI first. If they chose that order, the agent went on to the dispute and replacement jobs after the decision.
